translation_notes: four namespace terms become prefixed names in place: SDO.workExample -> sdo:workExample, RDF.type -> rdf:type, SDO.TextObject -> sdo:TextObject, SDO.ImageObject -> sdo:ImageObject. Everything else (the loop, the membership tests, the sort) is Python and is untouched.

only 2 of the 14 drafted @prefix declarations were kept (rdf, sdo); the other twelve namespaces are imported by the source file but unused in the region. The rdflib.namespace import block is left exactly as upstream.

FINDING: the region is a *read* path, and that is all ldpy can do for it -- there is no island for a triple-pattern read or for the 'is this class type present' test, so 'graph.objects(iri, sdo:workExample)' is as far as the notation goes. Note also that outside g{ } there is no 'a' shorthand, so RDF.type has to be spelled rdf:type.

SIDE OBSERVATION: SDO.TextObject makes rdflib emit 'UserWarning: Code: TextObject is not defined in namespace SDO' (DefinedNamespace validation), while sdo:TextObject resolves at transpile time to the same URIRef with no warning. Same term, but the island silently loses rdflib's typo checking on closed namespaces.

context shim (identical on both sides): supermodel_shim.py, because pylode/__init__.py imports 'dominate'. It copies MediaObject/ImageObject/TextObject (model.py lines 9-42) and get_value/get_text_object/get_image_object (query/__init__.py lines 68-135, module-level siblings that the region calls by name). The 14-name model import is trimmed to the single name the region uses (MediaObject) plus the two sibling functions.
driver fixtures: a container carrying one sdo:ImageObject and one sdo:TextObject example (the shape documented in the source file's own get_images docstring), and a subject with no example at all.
